route-btn.rule: the project route shifted toward black until white text clears 4.5:1; used for primary button faces

route-text.rule: the project route shifted toward black (day) or white (night) until it clears 4.5:1 on the ground; used for route-coloured text and link hover

route-soft.rule: hover wash, pressed state, agent avatar, route pill

route-line.value: day: color-mix(in srgb, var(--route) 85%, var(--ink)); night: color-mix(in srgb, var(--route) 80%, #ffffff)
route-line.rule: the rail, the track segments, the map route

headline.purpose: Page h1 on Projects and the project map; the only size above 15px in use.

title.purpose: Diagram title in the top bar and project row titles; the version number uses the same size at 700.

body.purpose: Base UI size; buttons and tab labels at 500; note bodies at 1.5 line-height.

meta.purpose: Readout, timestamps, descriptions, table cells, field labels, empty states.

label.purpose: Uppercase section headers in the panel and on pages; table headers at 11px.

micro.purpose: Pills and count badges; chips at 400, tags at 500, tooltips at 400.

mono.purpose: Only the context-digest <pre> on the project page.

shadows.name: shadow-float
shadows.purpose: Day: the scene banner, the toast, the ≤900px panel overlay. Nothing at rest.

shadows.name: shadow-float-night
shadows.purpose: Night value of the same token.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Input focus; a ring, not depth.

shadows.name: interchange-ring
shadows.purpose: The double ring on a linked station in the station line; a ring, not depth.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing; every transition and keyframe uses it.

motion.name: t-base
motion.purpose: Panel collapse, row rerank (view transition), toast-in.

motion.name: ride
motion.purpose: The train riding the station-line track on autosave.

motion.name: ring
motion.purpose: The map active-station ring expanding from r 9 to 22 and fading.

motion.name: view-transition
motion.purpose: Rows rerank in place (stops, notes); off under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: all durations 0.01ms; train and map marker hidden

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Top bar to two columns; station line and readout text hidden; panel becomes a right overlay (provisional).

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Map footer stacks; map key becomes a two-column grid.

breakpoints.name: page-max
breakpoints.purpose: Max content width on Projects and project map pages.

breakpoints.name: map-min
breakpoints.purpose: Minimum width of the transit map SVG; scrolls horizontally below it.

notCanonized: Project page boxes: .map-wrap, the conversation thread (inline style in ProjectPage.tsx) and .brain wrap content in 1px --rule borders with --radius-lg; the contract and the panel use hairline sections. Carried defect, not a rule.
Small-screen panel ships as an absolute right-edge overlay with --shadow-float at ≤900px; the contract listed a bottom sheet as unresolved. Provisional, not a rule.

narrative.overview:
The workbench is a transit system drawn with the fewest marks a map legend needs: a line, a dot, a ring, a dash. A project is a route in one saturated colour; each diagram is a station on it; a link is an interchange (a double ring on the line, a dashed arc on the map); a saved version is a stop behind you on the rail. The shell around the Excalidraw canvas is an ordinary editor shell (a 48px top bar, a docked 360px panel) and the world shows only through type, route colour, legend density and the station-line move. The hand-drawn canvas carries the personality; the chrome carries the wayfinding.

Density is timetable density: 13px UI type, 12px legend and meta, 11px pills, all in the Helvetica Neue / Helvetica / Arial system stack with tabular figures wherever a number appears. Surfaces are flat. Hairline (1px) rules divide the panel into sections; nothing is boxed; the one soft offset shadow belongs to things that float (the scene banner, the toast, the small-screen panel overlay). Day service is white; night service is near-black (#111316); both are tinted cool-neutral and the Excalidraw theme toggle drives them.

Rejections confirmed by the build: no cards on the panel, no second accent, no icon font or web font, no emoji glyphs, no modal for routine actions (confirm, restore and delete happen inline in the row), and no fades for content motion (motion travels along the line or reranks in place).
keyCharacteristics: One route colour per project is the only accent; state hues (green confirmed, amber unconfirmed, red error, gold newly arrived) mark state and nothing else.
Transit grotesk system stack on a 13 / 12 / 11px UI ramp, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` set on `body`.
Hairline-ruled sections, flat resting surfaces, one float shadow.
A diagram is always a station: white dot, 2px Signal Black ring; 3px route ring when on canvas; double ring when linked; dot size on a fixed ramp by element count.
Motion travels along lines: the train rides the track on autosave, the active station arrives once, rows rerank in place through view transitions.
An authored 16px / 1.5px-stroke inline SVG icon set, one weight, no icon font.

rules.name: The One Route Rule
rules.body: Every accent on a screen reads from `--route` or one of its derivations; there is no second accent, and the route changes only when the project does.

rules.name: The Fit-to-4.5 Rule
rules.body: A route colour never touches text or a button face raw: `routeTokens()` derives `--route-btn`, `--route-ink` and `--route-text` per theme until each pair clears 4.5:1.

rules.name: The State-Is-Not-Decoration Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, red and gold appear only on the thing whose state they report (a pill, a dot, a ring, a row tint); they never colour headings, layout or ordinary buttons.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: `body` sets `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`; every number (readout time, element counts, version numbers, stats) sits on tabular figures so rows rerank without jitter.

rules.name: The Headline Number Rule
rules.body: In a version row the number ("v7") is the headline at 15px / 700; its label sits beside it at 13px / 500 in Platform Grey, and nothing is labelled twice.

rules.name: The Hairline Section Rule
rules.body: Panel and page content is divided, not boxed: sections and rows end in a 1px `--rule` border and share the 16px gutter.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: `--shadow-float` goes on things that float (scene banner, toast, the small-screen panel overlay) and on nothing that rests.

rules.name: The Ring-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A `box-shadow` on a station or an input is a ring that reports state; it is never softened or offset into depth.

rules.name: The Station Mark Rule
rules.body: A diagram is always a white dot (`station-fill`) with a 2px Signal Black ring, sized 8 / 10 / 12 / 14px for 0 / ≤5 / ≤30 / >30 elements (`stationSize`); confirmed is a green ring, on canvas is a 3px route ring 4px larger, linked is a double ring. The map key draws the same marks it explains.

rules.name: The Along-the-Line Rule
rules.body: Motion travels along a line or reranks in place: the train rides the track, the station arrives, the ring expands, rows move to their new rank. Nothing fades in from nowhere except the toast, and nothing bounces.

dos: **Do** read every accent from `--route` and its derivations (`--route-btn`, `--route-ink`, `--route-text`, `--route-soft`, `--route-line`), set through `applyRoute(project.color, theme)`; a per-row route comes from `routeStyle()`.
**Do** divide panel and page content with 1px `--rule` hairlines (`.panel-section`, row borders) and keep resting surfaces flat on the ground / Rail Grey / Sunk Grey tone steps.
**Do** keep one control height: 30px for buttons, the readout and the route chip; 26px for `.btn-sm`; 32px minimum for inputs; 40px for tabs.
**Do** draw a diagram as a station: white dot, 2px Signal Black ring, sized 8 / 10 / 12 / 14px by element count, green when confirmed, 3px route ring when on canvas, double ring when linked.
**Do** use the authored 16px / 1.5px-stroke `Icon` set and add new glyphs to `icons.tsx` on the same grid and weight.
**Do** keep numbers in tabular figures and make the version number the row headline at 15px / 700.
**Do** hold the `--new-soft` tint on a newly arrived note or version until it is hovered or focused.
**Do** give focus a 2px route outline offset 2px, and inputs a route border with a 3px ring at 22% route.
**Do** confirm destructive or replacing actions inline in the row (small danger or primary button plus a ghost "Cancel") and report results in the toast.
**Do** move along the line: reuse `withViewTransition()` for reranking rows and the `--t-fast` / `--t-base` / `--t-slow` steps with `--ease-out`; honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: **Don't** add a second accent colour; green, amber, red and gold report state and appear only on the pill, dot, ring or row tint that carries it.
**Don't** box panel or page content in bordered, rounded cards; the 10px radius belongs to floating surfaces (scene banner, toast).
**Don't** put `--shadow-float` on anything at rest; it is for the scene banner, the toast and the small-screen panel overlay only.
**Don't** load a web font or an icon font, and don't use emoji or glyph characters as icons; the chrome is the Helvetica Neue / Helvetica / Arial stack with inline SVG.
**Don't** put a raw project colour on text or a button face; derive it through `routeTokens()` so every pair clears 4.5:1.
**Don't** cover or restyle Excalidraw's own chrome (toolbar, menus, shortcuts, theme); the shell wraps the canvas and only the scene banner floats over it.
**Don't** add a modal for routine actions (save, confirm, restore, delete, rename, link); they happen inline where the thing is.
**Don't** label twice: no eyebrow or kicker above a headline, no "Version" word beside "v7", no repeated section title inside a row.
**Don't** use `--fs-18` or `--fs-32` without a new reason; no shipped surface needs a size above 24px or between 15 and 24.
**Don't** animate content with fades, bounces or slides that do not follow a line or a rerank; the toast is the one allowed slide-in.
